info.title: ForgePilot orchestrator API
info.description: forgepilot-api/v1: the Node-to-UI contract of the ForgePilot pilot, the enterprise identity surface (DAT-202, ADR-0006), and the workspace, team, member, and invitation surface (DAT-205). The UI calls Node only; it never sees dsh sockets, boot tokens, Pi credentials, raw tool output, or provider credentials. Pi text is displayed only through the fail-closed pi_summary contract (DAT-191), whose classification boundary is DAT-192, whose trusted-source display boundary is DAT-193, and whose verifiable provenance record and read-side gate are DAT-194. Every error uses the shared versioned envelope (DAT-226 alignment, docs/contracts/error-envelope-v1.md vocabulary); authentication failures and cross-scope reads are non-enumerating; session invalidation terminates SSE subscriptions; and enterprise/workspace scope is always resolved server-side from authenticated membership — client-supplied identifiers never grant access. The collaboration surface (DAT-221, ADR-0007) defines durable issues, child tasks, bounded runs, immutable candidates, candidate-bound human pre-PR approvals, and broker-controlled deliveries; this contract is merged ahead of its serving implementation so dependent web work never invents fields, and it claims no running control until that implementation lands. Product stages and harness run states are separate vocabularies, and its outcome semantics are explicit: a `stopped` run or `needs_human` stop is a `stop` category — not retryable, requiring human disposition and a fresh run/grant; an `unknown` provider/delivery outcome is the `unknown` category — never auto-retried and requiring reconciliation before further writes; only service-decided bounded retries are `retry`, with `retryable` and `retry_after_seconds` on the shared envelope. Mutating collaboration commands are replay-safe by `Idempotency-Key`, and the issue SSE stream replays by `Last-Event-ID` with replay-stable event ids. client-supplied identifiers never grant access. Workspace memory (DAT-236) is bounded, cited, reproducible, and untrusted by construction: the bundle records the exact memory and retrieval-policy version it read, omits rather than dilutes, surfaces conflicts instead of overwriting, degrades to policy-only when the memory store is unavailable, and can never expand a capability grant — dsh remains the sole tool gate. Generated from the orchestrator implementation; shapes are defined by docs/contracts/forgepilot-api-v1.md.

post.summary: Create a task in one workspace
post.description: Creates the task and its dsh run inside the path workspace. The workspace's own binding supplies the repository, base revision, and model-gateway enterprise/workspace identity; the deployment's configured repository is never a fallback. `repository_id` must equal the workspace's repository binding (`400 REPOSITORY_NOT_IN_WORKSPACE`) and `base_ref` must equal that binding's pinned base revision (`400 BASE_REF_NOT_SUPPORTED`). Unknown/archived workspaces and non-members are one `404 NOT_FOUND`; viewers are `403 FORBIDDEN`. A workspace whose repository has no pinned base revision in this deployment is `409 REPOSITORY_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE`, and a provider instance that is no longer registered is `409 PROVIDER_INSTANCE_NOT_APPROVED`; both refuse before any dsh dispatch. Each workspace has its own idempotency-key namespace.

workspace_id.description: Durable workspace ownership. Always equal to the workspace in the scoped path; a task can never be addressed through another workspace's route family.

run_history_url.description: Relative run-history URL on the route family that served the task: `/api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/runs` on the legacy family and `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/tasks/{task_id}/runs` on the workspace-scoped family. Following it never crosses into another workspace's route family.

association.description: Verifiable task/run/repository/revision binding. run_id and head_sha are projected from the authoritative dsh run; task_id, repository_id, and base_sha are the creation bindings dsh accepted and pinned for the run. Node never invents any of these values.

archived.description: Whether the cancelled task is in the archive view; the run status is unchanged.

pi_summary.description: Display-safe summary of the latest settled Pi turn for the current run (DAT-191). Null until a Pi session exists for the task. The raw pi.text_delta stream is never the display source: text is exposed only through this fail-closed, Node-judged summary, and only with a verifiable source record (DAT-194) — a summary whose source cannot be re-proven, including every legacy DAT-191/192 record, is served unavailable with text null.

memory.description: Memory and retrieval-policy versions this run was pinned to at start (DAT-238), so a run is reproducible after a rollback. `canary` marks an unpublished candidate policy overlay; `item_ids` are the exact memory versions injected. Null when the memory service is not configured; `degraded` records an outage that did not block the run.

governance.description: GitHub merge-boundary projection for the current head. Approvals and checks observed against an older head are invalidated: observations_valid turns false and merge_queue_eligible turns false until dsh observes them against the current head.

PiSummary.description: A display-safe natural-language summary of the latest settled Pi turn for one task run (DAT-191, classification boundary DAT-192, trust boundary DAT-193, verifiable provenance DAT-194). Displayability comes from provenance, not text inspection: text is exposed only when it comes from an auditable trusted source whose composition is reviewable in the orchestrator, and free model output never has one — no rule table can prove that arbitrary free text contains no command — so a settled model turn is withheld in full. The Node-side fail-closed classifier still names why material is kept out: credentials, shell syntax, absolute workspace paths, command invocations, argument material, unredacted logs, and opaque high-entropy strings fail closed as unsafe_content; an execution report or a sentence/line opener it cannot recognise as narrative prose (capitalisation confers no exemption; every line start is judged) fails closed as undecidable; a turn no rule flags is withheld as untrusted_source — a pass of the rule table is a classification, not a certification. Fail closed: an unavailable summary always carries text=null, never redacted or partial content. The one available path (DAT-193) is the turn's validated structured Pi report: closed-enum parameters on the report_turn_summary tool, server-side validation, and fixed wording composed by Node and framed as Pi's own report — never free model text, never run status or activity counts, and no additional model, network, or permission. A missing, unknown, or invalid report fails closed exactly like a turn with no report. Provenance (DAT-194): `source` is the machine-checkable record behind that claim — closed channel, proof-format version, task/run/turn attribution, and the echoed structured report — non-null exactly when status is available. The server re-proves every served available summary from it and withholds anything it cannot prove: a missing or unknown source, an unknown version, attribution to a different task/run/turn, tampered text, or a damaged record all serve as unavailable/untrusted_source with text null. Nothing is inferred from the text's shape, a timestamp, or the service's current version; no persisted record or recorded event is rewritten, so legacy DAT-191/192 free-text summaries keep their history but are never served as displayable. Lifecycle: null on the task until a Pi session exists; pending from session start (and at the start of every run) until a turn settles; then exactly one available/unavailable per settled turn, each replacing the previous summary — a turn settles (and publishes) exactly once, including the duplicated agent_error/agent_settled emission of a provider failure. A terminal task whose last turn never settled keeps status pending with text null; no summary is fabricated after the terminal frame. A pi.summary.updated event carries the same object on the SSE stream and in the timeline, replayable by Last-Event-ID like every other event, and passes the same provenance gate, so projection and events always agree.

run_id.description: The run whose Pi session produced this summary.

turn_id.description: The Pi turn this summary describes; null while pending.

text.description: The fixed-wording rendering of the turn's validated structured Pi report (DAT-193), framed as Pi's own report; non-null iff status is available. Never free model text. Bound to 240 characters.

unavailable_reason.description: Why no text is exposed: no_content (the settled turn produced no displayable text), unsafe_content (identified unsafe material), undecidable (the classifier could not recognise the turn: an execution report or an unrecognised sentence opener), gate_error (the classifier itself failed), untrusted_source (no rule flagged the content, but it has no auditable trusted source: free model text, a structured report that failed server-side validation, or a recorded summary whose source cannot be re-proven on read — legacy, missing, forged, or unknown-version provenance). Null unless status is unavailable. The enum is additive: clients render an unknown reason — and an unknown status — as a plain unavailable state. A legacy available summary is served this way after the DAT-194 gate downgrades it, so an old client that renders on status and text alone stops displaying historical free text without understanding the source field.

source.description: Verifiable provenance of `text`; non-null iff status is available. Null for pending and unavailable summaries, and for any summary whose source the server cannot re-proven (which is then served unavailable with text null instead of exposing an unproven source).

PiSummarySource.description: Verifiable provenance of a displayable summary's text (DAT-194). Non-null exactly when the summary is available. The trust chain it states: `kind` is the closed provenance channel (only `turn_report` — the model's closed-enum report_turn_summary tool, validated by the server and fixed-rendered by the server), `version` versions the proof format and rendering vocabulary (carried by the record; an unknown version is unverifiable), task_id/run_id/turn_id bind the proof to the task, run, and turn the summary describes, and `report` echoes the validated closed-enum report the text was rendered from. The server re-proves every served available summary from this record — valid report, re-rendered wording equal to the stored text, identical attribution, known kind and version — and serves anything it cannot prove as unavailable/untrusted_source with text null. Legacy DAT-191/192 summaries carry no source and are therefore never served as displayable. A client MAY corroborate these fields (enums, attribution, version); that check is not the safety boundary.

kind.description: The provenance channel. Closed set: any other kind is not a trusted source and fails closed.

version.description: Version of the source proof format and its rendering vocabulary. This contract defines 1; a client MUST treat an unknown version as unverifiable, and the server serves such summaries as unavailable.

task_id.description: Task the proof is bound to.

run_id.description: Run the proof is bound to; must equal the summary's run_id.

turn_id.description: Pi turn the proof is bound to; must equal the summary's turn_id.

TurnReport.description: One validated structured Pi turn report: the closed-enum parameters of the report_turn_summary tool (DAT-193). Every parameter is a key from a closed vocabulary — there is no free-text field — and the server validates membership and cardinality before recording it. Summary text is fixed-rendered from exactly this structure.

RunSummary.description: One remediation run on a task. The optional evidence fields are written only while that run was active; absent means the evidence cannot be attributed to this run (DAT-238), never that it is zero.

actions_completed.description: Executed tool actions attributed to this run.

safety_events.description: Prohibited/policy-denied tool intents attributed to this run.

updated_at.description: Last time this run's own evidence changed.

User.description: An account, matched across providers only by (provider instance, stable subject). `identities` is the linked-provider provenance (DAT-203's views serve it); the core projection is served everywhere.

UserIdentity.description: A linked provider identity. Identity is bound by provider instance and stable subject ID — never by email address or blame author name (ADR-0006).

subject_id.description: Stable provider subject ID (e.g. the numeric GitHub account ID).

EnterpriseRef.description: The enterprise that owns the surrounding scope. Enterprises are represented explicitly even when a deployment serves exactly one.

Workspace.description: One workspace binds exactly one provider repository within one enterprise (ADR-0006). Within an enterprise an active workspace per repository is enforced transactionally.

role.description: The caller's effective workspace role, computed server-side from authenticated membership. A projection for display only — never an input, never authoritative from the client.

WorkspaceRepository.description: The workspace's provider repository binding: the provider instance and the immutable provider-assigned repository ID — never a mutable URL. Renames change metadata only; a transfer replaces this binding through the dedicated, authority-revalidated transfer operation.

Membership.description: A workspace membership. Effective access intersects enterprise membership, workspace role, current repository access, and action policy (ADR-0006); a role here is never sufficient authority on its own. The administrator grant response serves the core projection; the workspace-admin views (`GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members`, invitation redemption) additionally serve `user`, `authority`, `version`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`.

MemberAuthority.description: Provenance of the member's effective provider role (ADR-0006): how the provider conferred authority, when it was last verified, and whether it is stale. Missing or unverifiable provenance is `unknown`, never invented; stale or unknown authority blocks sensitive actions pending reconciliation (DAT-203).

provider_role.description: Normalized effective provider role label as reported by the provider adapter; null until verified.

stale.description: True when provider authority changed or went unverified and reconciliation has not confirmed it.

MemberCandidate.description: A provider-roster candidate for workspace membership (DAT-203): the eligibility view an owner/admin selects joins from. Roster completeness is fail-closed — incomplete rosters are an error, never an empty list.

ineligible_reason.description: Machine code naming why the candidate cannot be imported (e.g. `stale_authority`, `no_repository_access`); null when eligible. Additive vocabulary.

Team.description: A workspace team (ADR-0006). Teams are a routing signal, never an authorization source: team leadership or membership grants no repository access, security privilege, or delivery approval. Leaders must be active workspace members.

responsibility.description: Responsibility description or path mapping; null when unset.

Invitation.description: An owner-created invitation (ADR-0006). The bearer token is returned exactly once, by the create response only; every other view is token-free. An invitation grants nothing by itself: redemption adds a member-role membership only after login, explicit join confirmation, and live eligibility checks.

role.description: Invitations grant `member` only; administrative role elevation is a separate audited action after joining (ADR-0006).

bound_provider_subject.description: When set, only this verified provider subject may redeem the invitation; forwarded or wrong-subject use stays denied.

status.description: Server-computed state of this one-time invitation.

CreatedInvitation.description: The create response is the only place the bearer token ever appears.

token.description: The opaque bearer invitation: at least 128 bits of random entropy, URL-safe, stored server-side only as a keyed digest. Shown exactly once, in this response only — never in any later read, telemetry, referrer, error message, log, analytics export, or third-party asset. Both presentations convey this same value: the grouped copyable code is only a display formatting of it, and the QR encodes `invite_url`.

invite_url.description: Trusted-service invitation landing URL carrying the bearer in the URL fragment (`…#<token>`), never in the query. The landing page never consumes the token on GET — link previews and security scanners learn nothing — clears the fragment from browser history after capture, and submits the token only in an authenticated confirmation POST body (ADR-0006).

InvitationPreview.description: What the join-confirmation screen renders before the explicit join. Every non-consumable state fails exactly like redemption: one non-enumerating INVITATION_NOT_ACCEPTED.

already_joined.description: True when the caller already redeemed this invitation; redemption is then an idempotent replay of their own join, never a second join.

WorkspaceScope.description: The enterprise/workspace pair that owns an issue and everything derived from it (ADR-0006). Resolved server-side from the caller's authenticated membership; it is never accepted from a request body.

IssueRepository.description: Immutable repository identity an issue, its runs, candidates, and deliveries are bound to (ADR-0006 binds an id, not a mutable URL).

Digest.description: A digest value with the algorithm that produced it; an unverifiable or algorithm-less digest is never a valid evidence reference.

ArtifactReference.description: Immutable artifact reference (ADR-0007: handoffs carry artifact references and head identity, never raw memory). The digest binds the reference to exactly one artifact content; `base_sha`/`head_sha` bind it to the revision it was produced from.

Issue.description: A product issue (ADR-0007): the durable aggregate the workspace triages, plans, implements, validates, approves, and delivers. `product_state` is the product lifecycle stage — never a harness run state — and terminal stages (`completed`, `cancelled`) have no outgoing edge. `completed` requires a provider-confirmed merge; a published PR alone is not completion. `needs_human` records a stop reason awaiting human disposition, with other `needs_human` exits requiring that disposition.

dedupe_key.description: Service-derived fingerprint (versioned for log signals) that binds a repeated alert to one issue instead of spawning unbounded tasks; a repeat updates the existing issue's evidence.

source_reference.description: Immutable originating signal or manual submission reference.

state_reason.description: Recorded reason for the current product stage; always set for a `needs_human` stop and for an explicit cancellation.

IssueStage.description: The issue's product lifecycle stage and the stages it may move to next, derived from the ADR-0007 stage table. A transition is refused when the edge does not exist (409 TRANSITION_FORBIDDEN) or when the target stage is inconsistent with the observed harness states of the issue's runs (409 PRODUCT_HARNESS_CONFLICT). Leaving `needs_human` without a recorded human disposition is 428 DISPOSITION_REQUIRED.

allowed_transitions.description: Exact outgoing edges of the current stage; empty for terminal stages.

IssueTask.description: A child task of an issue: one bounded unit of work routed to a specific Pi role (ADR-0007), never an implicitly distributed squad. `depends_on` names tasks that must reach `done` first; a blocked dependency is 409 TASK_BLOCKED and an invalid dependency graph is 409 TASK_DEPENDENCY_INVALID.

RunWorktree.description: One run's isolated checkout. Different runs use separate worktrees; one worktree identity is never bound to two concurrent runs.

RunScope.description: Tool, path, and network scope recorded for one bounded run. Missing scope means denied: the scope narrows what dsh may grant, never widens it.

RunLimits.description: Duration, resource, and token limits recorded for one bounded run.

RunLease.description: Lease with a monotonic fencing token. Only the current holder of the current fencing token may mutate the run; a token is never reused, so a worker that lost its lease (expiry, crash, restart) can never overwrite a newer writer.

RunGrant.description: Capability grant recorded for one run (task-evidence-contract-v1 §2). The recorded grant mirrors what dsh issued and grants nothing by itself — dsh re-checks every operation. `state` is the effective state at read time: revocation is recorded and permanent, expiry is derived from the clock, and a stopped or terminal run's grants are revoked.

may_create_or_update_pr.description: Whether this grant permits PR creation; PR capability never includes merge, self-review, or check waiver, and delivery still requires a current candidate-bound human approval.

IssueRun.description: One bounded remediation run: isolated checkout, scope, limits, capability grants, lease, and the observed harness (FP-01) state. `state` is the harness state dsh reported and is never invented here. A `stopped` run requires human disposition and never resumes: it may become `cancelled`, or a new grant may move it to `approved` — stopped-to-running does not exist. `timed_out`, `expired`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, and `merged` are terminal for the grant; a later attempt is a new run id beginning in `requested`.

head_sha.description: Candidate head identity produced by the run so far; null until one exists.

stop_reason.description: Why the run stopped (validation failure, policy/security stop, resource violation, …). A stop is an outcome, not a retry: continuation needs human disposition and a fresh run/grant.

ValidationResult.description: One validation attempt against the exact candidate revision: the tool invoked, its redacted exit status, the digest of its redacted output, and the matching append-only event reference.

ChangeRisk.description: The pre-approval risk decision for the candidate's work. `prohibited` is never downgraded in the same run; an `elevated` assessment requires the recorded pre-grant human approval reference.

Candidate.description: An immutable frozen candidate (ADR-0007): the exact patch, revision identity, diff digest, changed paths, validation configuration/environment identity, test results, risk, and provenance a human reviews before any remote branch push or PR. Local preparation stops and the preparation run's grant is revoked while the candidate is preserved outside the ephemeral workspace. Nothing may be added or edited after validation, and no approval or delivery applies to any other revision. The review card shows `summary` and expands to the authorized diff (`diff`, artifacts), tests (`validation`), risks (`risk`), and provenance (`artifacts`, `audit_refs`).

run_id.description: The preparation run that produced the candidate.

diff.description: Digest and shape of the exact diff an approver reviews.

summary.description: Bounded change summary for the review card.

validation.description: The validation evidence the approval is bound to: configuration digest, environment identity, and every validation attempt.

required_checks.description: Validation identities of the run's approved test plan. The set must equal the registered test-policy checks the plan is bound to; every check needs a passing attempt backed by a retained execution artifact whose digest is the attempt's `output_digest`, produced from this exact revision. A failed, unexecuted, unplanned, or digest-mismatched check stops the run instead of producing a review card.

policy_id.description: The registered test-policy version this evidence is bound to. Required checks, config digest, and environment are policy content approved by a configuration administrator, never supplied by the run or the candidate.

policy_digest.description: Digest of the exact policy content, so an approval binds to that policy version even after a newer version becomes current.

artifacts.description: Patch, report, and evidence-bundle references, retained after cleanup.

audit_refs.description: References into the append-only audit/evidence records backing the candidate.

invalidated_at.description: When the candidate stopped being valid for delivery (base advancement, test-evidence, target, policy, or authority change). An invalidated candidate never authorizes delivery; a new revision needs a new run and a new candidate. Absent on records that predate this field and never invalidated.

invalidated_reason.description: Why the candidate was invalidated; always paired with `invalidated_at`.

ApprovalBinding.description: Everything one approval is bound to (ADR-0007). Content, required test evidence, base advancement, target, approval policy, expiry, or relevant authority changes invalidate the approval; refresh/rebase and rerun tests, then request a new card. Never rebase after approval and push under the old one.

target_branch.description: Intended PR target branch. Writes are restricted to the issue's autofixer branch and PR; direct main writes are never permitted.

ApprovalDecision.description: A recorded approver decision. The approver is the authenticated caller — never a body field — and the decision must be a confirmed mutation.

Approval.description: A candidate-bound pre-PR human approval request (ADR-0007). One named eligible human delivery approver — selected from workspace-configured maintainers — must approve the frozen candidate before any remote branch push or PR mutation; assignee/blame/team-leader status alone is insufficient, and current repository access plus explicit approval authority are checked. Approval is consumed by exactly one delivery operation; safe retries reconcile that same operation and never reuse the approval for a new candidate or PR. An approval never substitutes for the repository's own PR review, checks, or quorum.

approver.description: The named human the request is addressed to; null while no eligible approver is available (the issue then awaits human triage, never an automatic approval).

expires_at.description: Finite approval TTL; the proposed default is 24 hours.

Delivery.description: One broker-controlled delivery operation (ADR-0007). Only the trusted delivery broker obtains provider write credentials; before each write it re-checks current human approval, enterprise/repository permissions, the dsh grant, audit availability, branch constraints, and exact candidate identity. Operation identity and intention are persisted before the write; ambiguous push/PR outcomes are reconciled by branch and provider operation evidence before any retry, so a retry never merges, self-approves, or creates a duplicate PR. A pushed branch whose PR creation failed remains an explicit `partial` delivery — neither success nor automatic deletion. No state change deploys the change or claims the incident is fixed in production.

operation_id.description: Idempotent operation identity. Safe retries reconcile this same operation; they never authorize a new candidate or PR.

head_sha.description: The exact approved candidate commit published.

provider.description: Provider the broker writes through. GitLab delivery requires a reviewed mapping to that provider's repository governance before enablement; unsupported governance or missing integration permissions leave delivery blocked rather than silently advertised.

branch.description: The issue's autofixer branch once the push is verified; null before.

error_code.description: Safe machine code of the last provider failure (shared error vocabulary); raw provider text and credentials never appear.

reconciled_at.description: When the latest unknown/partial outcome was reconciled against provider evidence.

IssueEvent.description: One issue event on the SSE stream: the projection of exactly one durable audit record. Replay semantics: a reconnect sends the last delivered `event_id` in `Last-Event-ID`; the service replays every later event in `sequence` order from the durable projection (including events written while no client was connected, and across orchestrator restarts), so no business event is duplicated or lost. Delivery is at least once: `event_id` is stable and idempotent across replays — replayed frames carry the same id and payload — so a consumer MUST deduplicate on `event_id` and treat `sequence` as the ordering cursor. An unknown `Last-Event-ID` replays from the start of the retained log. The stream closes after `issue.terminal` is replayed, and a terminal issue's stream always closes after its replay even when the anchor is already at `issue.terminal`. A 404 ISSUE_NOT_FOUND is returned before any event is sent when the issue is not visible to the caller.

event_id.description: Stable, replay-stable event identity and the consumer's idempotency key. A new event never reuses an id; a replay never changes it.

sequence.description: Monotonic, gap-free order within the issue's event log.

csrf_token.description: Paired with the HttpOnly session cookie: cookie-authenticated mutating requests must echo it in the X-CSRF-Token header. It is readable by the page on purpose — possession without the cookie grants nothing.

origin_url.description: Administrator-approved provider origin. Registration enforces HTTPS, no credentials/path/query/fragment, the default port, and a public hostname or IP literal that resolves to public addresses only — internal-network origins are refused.

secret.description: Single-use desktop-held secret, returned exactly once at creation and exchanged once for the desktop session. It never appears in a URL, log, or audit record.

login_url.description: Open in the system browser to complete sign-in.

details.description: Secret-free detail; never carries tokens, codes, or states.

MemoryApplicability.description: Applicability of a memory item, and of a retrieval request's run context. An item field that is set only applies when the request field matches (path prefixes match on segment boundaries); empty means broad.

reference.description: Opaque pointer to a run, issue, PR, commit, test, reviewer decision, or incident. A citation is a provenance claim, not proof of correctness.

confidence.description: Support minus contradiction counts; may be negative.

trust.description: Provenance trust class plus evidence boost.

MemoryBundleItem.description: One injected memory item. Memory is untrusted data: this object can never grant a capability, approve a change, or authorize a tool action.

sensitivity.description: Retrieval applies the role's sensitivity ceiling; restricted items are never injected and require separate authorization.

approved.description: A named human approved this exact version. Facts and episodes are approved by validated promotion to active; procedural content needs a review stamp or human authorship.

candidate.description: Injected at reduced weight and labeled unapproved.

MemoryConflict.description: A visible contradiction. Neither side is injected as fact while the conflict is unresolved; a resolved conflict names the winning item.

MemoryBundle.description: Bounded, cited, reproducible memory context for one run. Mandatory L4 policy is never counted against the budget. A degraded bundle means memory was unavailable and the run proceeds with configured policy only. `memory_version` plus `policy_version` identify the exact memory a run read.

memory_version.description: Deterministic digest of the corpus the bundle read.

sparse.description: Fewer items than the eligible corpus warranted; omitted over diluted.

policy_items.description: Mandatory L4 policy; excluded from the token/item budget and never truncated. If the workspace policy corpus exceeds the supported bound, the request fails with a validation error instead of returning a bundle missing policy; that refusal is never reported as a degraded bundle.

candidates.description: Unapproved candidates at reduced weight, capped at two.

query.description: Task/issue text. Used for relevance only, never as authority.

context_window_tokens.description: Caller's model context window. Values below 1,000 are rejected rather than raised: the token budget is exactly 15% (or the policy share) of the stated window, never of a larger substituted one.

max_items.description: Clamped down to the policy bound and the hard ceiling.

policy_version.description: Pin a policy version to reproduce a historical run.

query_embedding.description: Query embedding produced through the model gateway (ADR-0005). The memory service never calls a model; absent means lexical-only scoring.

MemoryItemView.description: Human browse view of one memory item's current version. Reads are bounded and workspace-scoped; there is no cross-workspace browse.

MemoryVersions.description: Retrieval-policy versions plus the corpus digest and a bounded per-item version index for diffing. Version history is immutable; a bundle's `version` object names the exact pair it read. The index and corpus counts obey the caller's sensitivity ceiling: identifiers, versions, hashes, and timestamps of items the role cannot browse are not enumerable here. The ceiling is applied to every historical version's own sensitivity, so a restricted version stays hidden after the item's current version becomes internal.

MemoryEvalRunRequest.description: Evaluation result record. Recording a result never promotes memory; the RSI approval flow owns that decision. Evaluation cases cannot be written through this surface, and the hidden holdout stays read-only to the loop.

kind.description: The server-run replay is the only verifier; agent self-report is not a kind.

RsiCanaryObservation.description: One canary stage sample derived from pinned runs and their terminal task outcomes. Evidence is the server-generated pin set, never request text.

week_start.description: Monday of the ISO week (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

cases.description: Aggregate count only; holdout case content is never exposed.

RsiCreateProposalRequest.description: The proposer is the session user and the risk is derived from the target; neither may be sent. A retrieval-policy target carries `candidate_policy`; a memory-item target carries `memory_item` referencing a candidate version.

candidate_policy.description: Complete candidate retrieval policy. Validated against the same hard ceilings as a stored policy and unpublished until promotion.

RsiEvaluationRequest.description: Selects datasets only. The replay, its per-arm samples, delta, confidence interval, and verifier identity are computed or bound server-side; a request that carries metrics, a verifier claim, or evidence text is refused.

datasets.description: Defaults to both datasets; the canary gate requires both.

SecurityRuleScope.description: A rule correction is bound to exactly one enterprise and workspace.

internal.description: An internal endpoint is still scanned; internal never means exempt.

reason.description: Stable redacted reason. Never carries matched content.

safe_detail.description: Content-free handler summary; scrubbed at intake.

SecurityCase.description: Redacted case status. It contains no quarantined content and no credential: viewing raw context requires a separately granted, audited quarantine access.

note.description: Non-secret disposition note; scrubbed before it is recorded.

SecurityCaseTransitionRequest.description: Every edge requires its separated duty: handling and submission are handler work, review decisions are independent-reviewer work, and termination is handler or administrator work. Reviewing your own handling is rejected.

SecurityOwnerRequest.description: A task owner's request is recorded, never executed: only handler or administrator work dispositions a case.

SecurityQuarantineGrantRequest.description: Issued only by an enterprise security administrator, only to a handler or independent reviewer, and only for one record with an expiry. It is never a case reference and never a transferable credential.

content.description: Decrypted raw context. Returned only under a valid, scoped grant; this response is never logged, cached, or copied into an audit event, and the view attempt is audited whether it succeeds or is denied.

SecurityRuleConstraints.description: Narrowing constraints only. A correction can require more entropy, length, or a fixed marker; it can never disable a detector or widen what matches.

SecurityRegressionEvidence.description: Evidence the service computed from its trusted corpus. A proposal cannot submit evidence; activation re-verifies it.

SecurityRuleRevision.description: One versioned correction. A rule that selects one invocation, case, request digest, or secret value — or disables a whole detector — is rejected by name, not silently accepted.

SecurityRuleProposalRequest.description: The scope comes from the authenticated workspace path, never from the body. Regression evidence is computed by the service and cannot be supplied here.

SecurityRuleReviewRequest.description: Independent-reviewer work. A handler who authored or handled the change cannot review it, and role combinations never create an exception.

SecurityRuleActivationRequest.description: Enterprise-security-administrator work after an independent approval. Activation re-verifies the computed regression evidence; rollback cannot restore a superseded approval.

SecurityRecoveryApprovalRequest.description: Approves rechecking a rebuilt request at one destination — never a bypass. The approval binds the reviewed context revision, scope, destination, and current policy/rule/scan revisions, and expires.

context_revision.description: Keyed identifier of the complete reviewed request.

SecurityRecoveryApproval.description: An approval is not a dispatch. `state: approved` authorizes one recheck attempt; sending is recorded separately as a dispatch outcome.

SecurityRecoveryDispatchRequest.description: The complete request is rebuilt from approved sources and rechecked under current authorization, destination, classification, minimization, and secret rules. Any difference from the approved revisions invalidates the authorization (RECOVERY_APPROVAL_INVALID).

request_digest.description: Keyed digest of the exact frozen request handed to the adapter.

SecurityRecoveryDispatch.description: `unknown` means the provider outcome could not be established: the authorization is consumed and the request is never automatically replayed. An approval and an actual send are distinct audit events.

protected_refs.description: Keyed identifiers for content correlation. Never raw content and never a plain hash of a low-entropy secret value.

SecurityAuditEvent.description: One hash-chained, non-secret security audit event. Reading or exporting the trail records its own `audit.trail_read` / `audit.trail_exported` event with the requester and stated purpose.

purpose.description: Non-secret stated purpose, recorded with the export event.

SecurityAuditExportRequest.description: Restricted to the enterprise security administrator. The export is recorded as `audit.trail_exported` before the payload is returned, and no secret ever appears in it.

error.description: The shared versioned error envelope (ADR-0008, DAT-226 alignment): a stable machine code, the processing stage, the outcome category, a safe localizable user message, service-decided retryability, retry-after where applicable, the request_id trace/case reference, safe-only structured details, and the authorized next action. No field ever carries secrets, credentials, invitation tokens, or sensitive diagnostics; those stay behind separate access checks.

envelope_version.description: Envelope format version. Evolution within a version is additive only; a new version signals a breaking envelope change.

code.description: Stable machine code. Never localized and never re-mapped to a different meaning; display text lives in `message`. Unknown codes render from `message` plus `next_action`.

stage.description: The processing stage that rejected the request.

category.description: Outcome semantics: denial (refused by authority/policy; do not retry), stop (fix the request or state; do not retry), retry (a retry may succeed within limits), unknown (reconcile before further writes). The service, never a model or a client, decides retry eligibility; a policy denial is never rewritten as a generic server error.

message.description: Safe user-facing guidance. Localizable without changing `code`; a trace ID alone is never the only guidance. An unexpected INTERNAL_ERROR serves one fixed safe message; its cause stays in server-side logs, correlated by `request_id`.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before a retry; non-null when applicable (typically 429 and retryable 503), matching the Retry-After header where the server sends one.

request_id.description: Trace/case reference to quote in support and security cases.

case_ref.description: Authenticated security-case identifier, when the failure belongs to one (ADR-0005). A correlation handle only: it authorizes nothing and never grants access to quarantined content.

trace_ref.description: Trace identifier for correlation, when one exists.

details.description: Safe structured context only (e.g. a conflicting version, a denied capability category). Never secrets, raw provider errors, invitation tokens, or sensitive diagnostics.

next_action.description: The authorized next action, as a machine code. Additive vocabulary: a client renders an unknown action as generic guidance from `message`. Null when no action applies.

bearerAuth.description: Authorization: Bearer <token>. Either the per-process API token, minted at orchestrator start and written 0600 to the API token file (possession authorizes acting as the local operator, approvals included), or a desktop session token issued by the single-use desktop exchange. Web clients use the session cookie instead.

sessionCookie.name: fp_session
sessionCookie.description: Server-side web session in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie. Cookie-authenticated mutating requests must echo the session's CSRF token in the X-CSRF-Token header. Logout, suspension, and membership revocation invalidate it immediately.

bootstrapToken.name: X-Bootstrap-Token
bootstrapToken.description: Deployment-owned bootstrap secret (FORGEPILOT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN). The only authority for the first provider-instance approval and the one-time first-enterprise-administrator grant; every use is audited and the token never appears in logs or audit details.
